# Platform Updates: Viant Launches CTV Attention Targeting & Reporting


October 19, 2026 in[Blog](https://www.viantinc.com/insights/blog/)


***Platform Updates*** *is a new Viant Blog series exploring how the products and capabilities within the Viant Advertising Platform help marketers navigate their media with greater intelligence, transparency, and control to achieve stronger outcomes.*


## Key Takeaways: Making Attention Signals Actionable Across CTV Campaigns


- Viant has launched attention targeting, powered by TVision, making it the first platform to offer attention-based targeting for CTV directly in its buying workflow.
- Advertisers can target or exclude high, medium, and/or low attention categories, which represent the top, middle, and bottom thirds of measured attention.
- To measure the impact of attention based optimization, Viant provides advertisers with a CTV Attention Report. Available to all CTV customers at no additional cost, this report shows attention rate, attention index, co-viewing, presence in room, and attention-adjusted CPM (aCPM).
- aCPM helps advertisers understand the value of their media investments in a new way by comparing the cost of an impression to the cost of reaching an attentive, co-viewing audience.


---


What is a 30-second spot worth if nobody’s around to see it, or if nobody’s paying attention to it?


Picture a Monday night NFL game streaming at a group of friends’ apartment. As the group ventures into the kitchen to retrieve the platefuls of buffalo wings that just finished in the oven, a beautifully crafted, 30-second[CTV](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/omnichannel/connected-tv/) commercial simultaneously plays to the living room…with absolutely nobody in it. The advertiser’s reporting will say the impression was served, but an empty couch won’t remember that brand, and it certainly won’t be buying any products from it.


This happens more than anyone would like to admit. Research from[TVision](https://www.tvisioninsights.com/) shows that in 30% of instances, the room is empty while an ad plays. And even when someone is there, they’re not paying attention 45% of the time. Advertisers can prove an ad was served, but two questions have gone long unanswered: can a campaign target viewers who are actually paying attention? And can it show that attention was earned?


Viant is closing that gap through the launch of CTV Attention Targeting and the CTV Attention Report, making Viant the first platform to offer attention-based targeting natively in the buying process.


## Meet TVision, the Engine Behind the Attention


The data behind this launch is powered by TVision,[which Viant acquired in the spring of 2026](https://www.viantinc.com/company/news/press-releases/viant-announces-agreement-to-acquire-tvision-strengthening-its-ai-powered-programmatic-platform/) . TVision is the only attention measurement provider delivering second-by-second, eyes-on-screen attention, co-viewership, and in-room presence for TV. Its nationally representative panel of households is weighted to represent the US population and uses passive in-home hardware, advanced computer vision, and Automatic Content Recognition (ACR) technology to measure three things: whether someone’s in the room, whether multiple people are watching together, and whether they are actually paying attention.


Importantly, TVision doesn’t only watch one corner of the television ecosystem. TV advertising now spans linear, YouTube, Prime Video, and streaming apps, and many of those platforms grade their own homework. TVision’s panel captures real viewer engagement across that entire ecosystem, giving advertisers a single, independent, and market-wide view of attention.


## Shape the Buy Before the Impressions Run


Viant clients can now target attention as a top-level category in the DSP, directly within the CTV buying workflow. Here’s how it works:


- **Three categories:** Pick from High, Medium, and Low Attention, representing the top, middle, and bottom thirds of measured attention.
- **Target or exclude:** Use any category either way, depending on the goal.
- **Dynamic, not fixed:** Categories are recalculated dynamically, so advertisers are always buying against today’s attention landscape, not an outdated benchmark.
- **Built into the buy:** Attention is applied right on the CTV line, and delivery shows up in TVision measurement reporting, ensuring targeting and results stay connected.


Which setting fits best depends on individual campaign goals. A brand focused on maximizing active viewing can lean into High Attention, and an advertiser who wants to balance engagement and reach might test Medium Attention or mix levels. And for those who would rather stop paying for the moments no one is watching, they can exclude Low Attention.


Optimizing for attention in the targeting stage of the campaign is a worthwhile effort: a report from[TVision and Upwave](https://info.tvisioninsights.com/tvision-upwave-report) found that a 1% increase in attention is associated with a 1% increase in awareness and ad recall.


## Measure What Your Attention Actually Earned


Targeting gets attention into the buy, and the CTV Attention Report shows what it delivers. This report is available to all CTV customers at no additional cost for the rest of 2026, and running attention targeting is not required to use it. To locate it in the Viant platform, go to Performance > CTV Attention (labeled as “CTV Attention Powered by TVision”). This report is complimentary for all clients through the end of 2026.


Inside, buyers will find:


- **Core attention metrics:** attention rate, attention index, co-viewing, and presence in room.
- **Attention-adjusted CPM (aCPM):** standard CPM next to the cost of reaching attentive, co-viewing audiences, trended over time.
- **Top performers:** breakdowns by streaming app, daypart, day of week, and ad duration, to help identify which apps earn the most attention and which creative lengths hold a viewer’s focus.
- **Flexible granularity:** advertiser, campaign, order, and line level, with a 90-day lookback and a two-day data lag.


aCPM is an incredibly valuable metric, because it changes how buyers value inventory and plan campaigns. For example, Publisher 1 may have a $25 CPM with a 50% attention rate and 1.3 co-viewing, while Publisher 2 has a $30 CPM with a 55% attention rate and 1.6 co-viewing. On sticker price, Publisher 1 wins, but aCPM (CPM ÷ \[attention rate × co-viewing\]) comes out to $38.50 for Publisher 1 and $34.10 for Publisher 2. The “pricier” pick is actually the better value per attentive viewer.


## Served Was Never the Same as Seen


For a long time, “served” was as far as proof went. With attention targeting to aim the buy and the CTV Attention Report to check the result, advertisers can finally steer spend toward moments when people are present and watching.


***Ready to try it*** ***?** Talk to your Viant rep to start testing TVision Attention Targeting, and open the CTV Attention Report today.*

## Frequently Asked Questions


What is a cookieless DSP?Expand


A cookieless DSP is a programmatic advertising platform that identifies and reaches audiences using durable, privacy-first identifiers rather than third-party cookies.


Instead of relying on fragile browser tracking, these platforms leverage advanced solutions like Household ID™ to maintain scale and precision. This approach ensures that digital campaigns remain effective and measurable regardless of evolving browser restrictions or privacy regulations.


How does programmatic advertising work without cookies?Expand


Programmatic advertising functions without cookies by activating first-party data through identity resolution frameworks like Unified ID 2.0 and the Household ID. Marketers also utilize contextual targeting to align ads with real-time content and prioritize natively cookieless channels such as CTV and DOOH. These methods allow for high-impact reach and frequency management without the need for invasive user-level tracking.


What is the difference between a DSP and a cookieless DSP?Expand


Traditional DSPs rely on syncing third-party cookies across exchanges to build audience profiles, a process that is increasingly fragmented and unreliable. A cookieless DSP uses people-based identity, first-party data, and privacy-safe signals to reach consumers across all devices.


Viant DSP was purpose-built to be cookieless from the ground up, ensuring it never relied on the legacy infrastructure of third-party cookies.


What targeting options are available in a cookieless environment?Expand


Marketers in a cookieless environment can utilize a robust suite of options including contextual targeting, first-party data onboarding, and household-level identity resolution.


Furthermore, interoperability with alternative ID frameworks like Unified ID 2.0 allows brands to maintain significant scale across the open web. These diverse tactics provide a durable, privacy-forward alternative to outdated cookie-based audience segments.


How is campaign performance measured in a cookieless world?Expand


In a cookieless world, campaign measurement is achieved through modern attribution models such as[incrementality testing](https://www.viantinc.com/insights/blog/incrementality-and-incrementality-testing-a-primer/) , Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM), and secure data clean rooms.


The Household ID serves as a critical cross-device attribution layer, linking high-impact exposures on CTV to conversions on other digital devices within the home. This transition allows advertisers to prove ROI and optimize spend without relying on fragmented, cookie-based signals.
